coverage_note: The readable opening sets up how to attack 'which implication is not true' questions and identifies the first question as GATE 1996, with option A (X and (X -> Y)) -> Y recognised as modus ponens and hence a tautology. The remaining options and the rest of the lecture were past the cut.
concepts: An implication alpha -> beta is false exactly when alpha is true and beta is false at the same time; if such an assignment exists the implication is not a tautology.
Every implication option in a 'which is not true' question is checked by hunting for that single falsifying assignment.
Modus ponens, (X and (X -> Y)) -> Y, is identified as a tautology.
The instructor's everyday test for a false implication: 'if you are Indian then you are Rajasthani' is false because the antecedent can hold while the consequent fails.
gate_claims: Instructor states the opening question is GATE 1996. This repository did not open the 1996 paper, so no PYQ record is created from it.
